crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Thematic Coding
children.blurb: Thematic coding is the qualitative research practice of sorting segments of text, transcript, image or field note into named categories so that patterns across a corpus can be described and compared.

children.name: Interview Transcription and Speaker Separation
children.blurb: Interview transcription and speaker separation covers the conversion of recorded speech into written text and the labelling of who said what in a multi person conversation.

children.name: Finding Patterns in Lived Experience
children.blurb: Finding Patterns in Lived Experience covers the qualitative and mixed methods work of turning interviews, diaries, focus groups and open survey answers into themes, codes and narratives.

children.name: Ethnographic Synthesis
children.blurb: Ethnographic synthesis is the practice of combining findings from multiple ethnographic or qualitative field studies into a single comparative account.

children.name: Combining Qualitative and Quantitative Data
children.blurb: Combining qualitative and quantitative data is the practice of bringing interview transcripts, field notes, open survey answers and other text or media together with counts, scores and measurements in one study.

sections.body: Qualitative analysis and mixed methods cover the work of turning interviews, field notes, open ended survey answers and other unstructured material into findings that can be compared and checked. In practice, AI is used to transcribe recorded interviews, separate speakers, suggest first pass codes, group those codes into candidate themes and summarise long transcripts. It also helps merge qualitative themes with quantitative variables so a study can report both a pattern and the numbers behind it. The aim is not to replace the researcher's judgement but to cut the mechanical load of sorting and labelling large text sets.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Transcription is the most settled part. Speaker separation works well on clear two person recordings and degrades with overlapping speech, heavy accents, poor microphones and specialist vocabulary. Thematic coding is partly solved at the level of suggestion. Models can propose codes and cluster them, but they cannot decide what a code means in a given study, and they tend to flatten minority or contradictory accounts. Ethnographic synthesis remains the weakest area because it depends on context, history and the researcher's presence in the field, none of which sit in the transcript. Combining qualitative and quantitative data is procedurally possible but conceptually hard, since the two traditions make different assumptions about what counts as evidence. Nothing here is advice, and no output should be treated as a finished finding without human review.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages run from raw material to combined design. Interview Transcription and Speaker Separation is the entry point, covering how audio becomes text and where that text loses fidelity. Thematic Coding takes the transcript and deals with labels, codebooks and consistency between coders. Finding Patterns in Lived Experience steps back from individual codes to look for recurring shape across many accounts. Ethnographic Synthesis handles the longer, context heavy work of building an account of a setting rather than a set of themes. Combining Qualitative and Quantitative Data closes the section by showing how themes and variables are brought into one study. A reader should start with transcription for practical setup, move to coding for method, and use the last three pages for design decisions about scope and integration.
